title: Helios Health customer story (draft outline v0) — Redwood Private (VPC) deployment for regulated workloads
body:
Working doc (v0). Goal: outline a compliance-safe public customer story for Helios Health focused on Redwood Private (VPC) deployment, auditability, and reliability controls. This version intentionally avoids regulated-claims language (e.g., “HIPAA compliant”) until Legal signs off.

OWNER / NEXT STEPS
- Writer: Ethan Wallace
- Messaging + narrative: Soojin Lee
- Technical validation: Markus Klein / Simran Kaur
- CS readiness + approvals: Rachel Kim
- Legal review: Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes

Status / open items
- [ ] Confirm final permissions: name/logo vs anonymized (“Helios Health” vs “a healthcare analytics provider”).
- [ ] Confirm what we can say about PHI: default assumption is “no PHI sent to Redwood” unless Helios explicitly approves different language.
- [ ] Resolve audit log phrasing and retention statements (see SUP-3890).
- [ ] Confirm which metrics can be public (exact vs range vs qualitative).

ONE-LINE SUMMARY (DRAFT)
Helios Health deployed Redwood Private in their VPC to run LLM workloads with strong auditability and operational controls—without sacrificing latency and uptime targets required for regulated environments.

PUBLIC-FACING POSITIONING (COMPLIANCE-SAFE)
Approved-ish claim style (do not overpromise):
- “Deployed inside Helios Health’s VPC with customer-managed networking controls.”
- “Integrated with customer key management for encryption key control.”
- “Enabled audit logs for inference activity and operational events.”
- “Used reliability features (routing policies, fallbacks, and capacity controls) to maintain service continuity.”

Avoid (unless Legal approves specific wording):
- “HIPAA compliant,” “HITRUST certified,” “BAA-covered by default,” “certified for PHI,” “meets all regulatory requirements.”
- Absolute security claims: “fully secure,” “guaranteed,” “cannot be accessed.”

PLACEHOLDERS FOR CUSTOMER CONTEXT
Company: Helios Health (TBD: public name vs anonymized)
Industry: Healthcare (regulated environment)
Region(s): TBD (confirm if we can mention)
Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC)
Primary interface: Chat/text generation (TBD)
Model(s): TBD / avoid naming if it increases review time

TARGET AUDIENCE
- Enterprise platform / infrastructure teams in healthcare + adjacent regulated verticals
- Security and compliance stakeholders evaluating LLM inference deployment models
- Engineering leaders who need predictable reliability (SLOs) + operational tooling

STORY ANGLE OPTIONS (PICK 1–2)
A) “Private deployment without losing velocity”
- Why: Helios needed VPC deployment + audit controls; they still wanted a developer-friendly API and fast iteration.

B) “Auditability + key control for inference”
- Why: Requirements around logging, retention, and encryption key ownership were gating vendor selection.

C) “Reliability under strict change control”
- Why: Regulated ops means fewer emergency changes; they needed guardrails like fallbacks and stable rollouts.

PROPOSED CASE STUDY STRUCTURE

1) Executive summary (top of page)
- What Helios built: (one sentence) e.g., “LLM-assisted clinician support workflow” or “patient support and knowledge retrieval assistant.”
- Why Redwood: private deployment + auditability + reliability controls.
- Outcome: improvement in operational confidence + ability to move to production under security constraints.

Draft summary paragraph:
Helios Health needed to run LLM inference under strict security and audit requirements. Redwood worked with Helios to deploy Redwood Private inside their VPC, integrating with their key management approach and enabling audit logs for inference operations. With reliability controls such as routing policies and fallbacks, Helios was able to meet internal launch requirements and operate the service with predictable performance and clear operational visibility.

2) The challenge (problem statement)
Prompts for interview / content:
- What was the initial use case? What user population? (internal staff vs external users)
- What were the blockers with hosted-only solutions?
- What did security/compliance require before launch?

Compliance-safe phrasing:
- “Helios operates in a regulated environment and needed deployment controls aligned with internal security review.”
- “They required network isolation, controlled access, and auditability for production operations.”

3) Requirements & constraints (make this a callout box)
Bullets (draft):
- Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed networking boundaries
- Key management integration expectations (customer-controlled keys; confirm exact integration)
- Audit logs: required fields, export format expectations, retention needs (do not state durations unless approved)
- Reliability requirements: uptime targets, incident response expectations, and operational escalation paths
- Data handling constraints: confirm what data types were allowed; default to “no sensitive patient data” unless explicitly approved

Optional (only if approved):
- Data residency constraints
- Access controls / SSO / RBAC requirements

4) Why Redwood (solution overview)
Focus on platform capabilities, not model hype.

Key points to cover:
- Redwood Private: control plane + runtime deployed within customer environment (VPC)
- Consistent API surface compared to hosted (reduced dev friction)
- Observability and operational hooks
- Reliability controls: routing policies, fallbacks, rollout policies

Suggested copy (draft):
Redwood Private allowed Helios to run inference within their own VPC while keeping a consistent developer experience. The deployment supported Helios’s security review by aligning network boundaries and access controls with their internal requirements, while Redwood’s operational features helped the team manage reliability and performance in production.

5) Implementation details (what we’ll validate with Solutions Eng)
This section should be concrete but not expose sensitive architecture details.

Implementation outline:
- Environment: Helios VPC
- Connectivity: private networking between Helios services and Redwood runtime endpoints (avoid exact topology unless approved)
- Authentication/authorization: (TBD) service-to-service auth + role-based access for Console/admin
- Key management: KMS/HSM (TBD) integration; confirm if “customer-managed keys” is accurate
- Logging/audit:
  - What events are logged? (admin actions, model/config changes, inference request metadata, error events)
  - Export path (to Helios SIEM / log storage) — keep vendor names out unless approved
- Reliability controls:
  - Routing policies (e.g., “fallback to compatible model variant”)
  - Capacity controls / autoscaling policy (avoid exact GPU counts)
  - Rollout strategy (canary / staged) and rollback procedure

Architecture diagram (needed):
- Minimal diagram: Helios App → Redwood Private Endpoint (VPC) → GPU runtime → Logs/metrics export → Helios logging system
- Do NOT include: IP ranges, account IDs, exact region names, internal hostnames

6) Results (metrics + proof)
We need to be careful: Helios may only approve qualitative outcomes or ranges.

Results options (use what they approve):
- Reliability / operational:
  - “Met internal launch criteria for uptime and incident response readiness.”
  - “Reduced on-call load / fewer production escalations” (only if they can back it up)
- Security/compliance readiness:
  - “Completed security review with deployment inside VPC and audit logging enabled.”
- Performance:
  - p95 latency range (TBD)
  - throughput improvement vs baseline (TBD)
- Cost:
  - $/1M tokens range or directional (“lowered unit cost”) (TBD)

Proof notes (internal):
- Identify measurement period (e.g., 30-day window post-launch)
- Ensure we can explain methodology in one sentence
- If any incident occurred during the measurement window, confirm exclusion rationale and have Support/SE signoff

7) Quote blocks (2–3)
We should aim for:
- 1 quote from Engineering/ML lead (implementation + performance)
- 1 quote from Security/Compliance/IT (auditability + key control)
- Optional: product owner quote (time-to-value)

Draft quote prompts (not final wording):
- “Deploying inside our VPC and aligning with our audit requirements was non-negotiable. Redwood helped us get there without slowing our team down.”
- “We needed predictable operations—clear logging, controlled access, and reliability mechanisms we could trust in production.”

8) What other teams can learn (practical takeaways)
Bullets:
- Align early on what “audit logs” means (fields, retention, export path)
- Decide what data is permitted for inference and document it
- Use staged rollouts + fallback policies for production stability
- Treat performance targets and reliability targets as a single launch gate

9) CTA / Sales enablement note
Public CTA:
- “Talk to us about Redwood Private deployments” + link
Internal enablement:
- This story should support late-stage Private evaluations with security gating.

COMPLIANCE / LEGAL REVIEW CHECKLIST (INTERNAL)
- Naming: can we use “Helios Health” publicly? If no, define the anonymized descriptor.
- Logos: allowed? (where: website, PDF, decks)
- Quotes: must be attributed? job title allowed?
- Metrics: exact vs range; if range, define acceptable banding.
- Disclosures: confirm any required disclaimers about customer-controlled environment.
- Prohibited topics: patient data, specific clinical workflows, vendor names, internal incident details.

INTERVIEW QUESTION BANK (FOR NEXT CUSTOMER CALL)
1) What problem did you start with, and what made it “regulated” from an ops perspective?
2) Which deployment requirements were hard blockers?
3) What was your internal approval workflow (security/compliance/procurement) and what evidence did you need?
4) What audit events did you need to capture and why?
5) What key management requirements did you have (control, rotation, separation of duties)?
6) What reliability targets mattered most (uptime, error rate, p95 latency, incident response)?
7) What did the first 30 days in production look like? Any surprises?
8) What would you tell another healthcare platform team evaluating inference vendors?

NOTES / RISKS
- Helios is likely to request anonymization and limited metrics disclosure; design the story to work even with 0 numeric metrics.
- Security phrasing must be precise. We should route final copy through Legal + Security for verification.
- Keep architecture diagram intentionally generic; Helios may require it to be reviewed line-by-line.

APPROVAL PLAN (DRAFT)
- Internal: PMM + Solutions Eng signoff on technical claims → Legal signoff on permissions/claims → Exec approval if needed for incentives.
- Customer: provide a single doc for review with tracked changes; propose 10 business day window; allow one revision cycle.

DISTRIBUTION (IF/WHEN APPROVED)
- Website case study page + PDF one-pager
- Sales talk track: “Private deployment + auditability” slide
- Optional: webinar/panel only if Helios explicitly opts in

END
